resources.string: A gentle space to track your little one\'s first weeks — and to look after you, too.\n\nLet\'s set things up. It\'ll only take a moment.
So we can greet you properly each day.
Would you like a daily check-in?
A card on your dashboard for how you\'re doing — never a notification. You can change this anytime in Settings.
You can always change this later in the profile.
This just tailors your daily check-in. Everything is optional.
This just tailors the wellbeing entries you add yourself. Everything is optional.
Adds gentle questions about your healing and bleeding.

A quiet moment for you, whenever you\'re ready.

How is your healing coming along?
Let\'s take a moment for you — just a few quick questions, one at a time.

No babies yet — add your little one to start tracking.
Their history is kept. Restore to track again.
This permanently removes %1$s and every feeding, sleep, diaper and growth entry for them. This can\'t be undone.
No treatments yet. Add one with the + button — e.g. Vitamin D every day.
Its reminders stop and the treatment is removed for good. This can\'t be undone.
Reminders to give your baby their treatments
Nothing set up yet. Add a medicine with the + button — a name and the wait you were told to keep between doses.
The medicine and the doses you logged for it are removed for good. This can\'t be undone.
From your prescriber or the leaflet. Sprout doesn\'t know this medicine or your baby — it only counts the hours you enter here.
Remind me when it can be given again
Can be given — %1$s before the usual wait
Leave the wait blank if you weren\'t given one — some medicines only cap how many, or how much, in a day.
Only if your leaflet gives a quantity — 1.5 cm of gel, 2.5 ml. Sprout adds up what you log and counts it against the daily maximum you type here.
Day\'s amount used up — %1$s to wait
Reminders that an as-needed medicine can be given again
This can be given again now.
This can be given to %1$s again now.
Nudge me when it\'s been too long since a feed.
A card on your dashboard for how you\'re doing — Sprout never interrupts you for it. Turn it off and the check-in disappears; your past entries are kept.
Choose which questions your check-in asks. Opting out of a question skips it every day; you can bring it back here anytime.
Remind me if a feed is more than
Reminders when it\'s been a while since the last feed
It\'s been %1$s since the last feed.
Babies often go through a growth spurt %1$s. Extra hunger, more waking and fussiness are normal — it usually passes in a few days.
A growth spurt is common %1$s — it may start in the next few days.
Give me a heads-up when a typical growth spurt period begins.
A running feed in the notifications

While a breastfeed is being timed, show it in the notifications with Pause, Switch side and Stop & save, so you don\'t have to unlock the phone. Your baby\'s name stays off the lock screen unless your phone shows all notification content.
A running feed on the lock screen

While a breastfeed is being timed, show it on the lock screen and in the Dynamic Island with Pause, Switch side and Stop & save, so you don\'t have to unlock the phone. It never shows your baby\'s name.
A breastfeed while it is being timed, with buttons to pause it, switch side and save it
On a break · %1$s at the breast
A heads-up when a typical growth spurt period begins
A growth spurt may be starting
%1$s may be starting a growth spurt
Growth spurts are common %1$s. Extra feeds and fussiness are normal — it usually passes in a few days.
The last feed — which baby, what kind, and how long ago — plus which breast the last breastfeed started on, or the breastfeeding session in progress with its live timer.
Couldn\'t draw the widget. Open Sprout, or remove and add it again.
Share this baby\'s record with the other people looking after them — no account, no cloud.
Choose which logs the home screen shows, and in which order.

Put the logs you use most first, and switch off the ones you don\'t use. Nothing is lost: a log that\'s switched off waits under More at the end of the grid, keeps sharing with your household\'s phones, and still counts in Trends and in the record for your doctor.
One record, every phone in the household

Invite the other parent — or a grandparent who has the baby regularly. Once a phone has joined, everyone can send their entries across and Sprout merges them: no account, no server, and nothing kept anywhere but your own phones.
Open an invitation I was sent

The invitation carries the key to your record, and anyone who has it can read and add to everything shared. Send it through something private — a messaging app, Quick Share, Bluetooth — and not anywhere public.
Every phone in the household shows these same six characters. Read them to each other once: a phone showing something else is not in your household.
Open a file I was sent
Send to each other in both directions to bring every phone up to date. Opening the same file twice changes nothing.
Your pumping log and the milk stash, shared with the whole household or with nobody. Everything about the baby is shared either way.
Turning this off stops future sends. What you have already sent stays on the other phone.
This phone will stop sending and opening the household\'s files. Everything already saved here stays.
Your household code is %1$s. Check that the other phones show the same one.
Joined %1$s\'s household. Your code is %2$s — check that the other phones show the same one.
Nothing new — both phones already agreed.
This file is not a Sprout invitation or a Sprout export.
This file was not sent by a phone in your household, or it was damaged on the way.
This file was written by a newer version of Sprout. Update the app and try again.
This invitation has expired. Ask for a new one.
Each phone has been tracking on its own, and Sprout cannot tell which entries are the same moment. Keep everything — anything logged twice will appear twice — or share only from now on?
No other phone has sent anything yet. Each one appears here the first time it does.

Removing a phone changes the household\'s key, so every other phone needs a new invitation too — including any that is switched off right now. The removed phone keeps what it already has; nothing can take that back.
Your new code is %1$s. Send a fresh invitation to everyone who stays — until you do, their phones cannot read what you send.
When you open Sprout, look for the household\'s phones nearby over Bluetooth and exchange with them. It only looks while the app is open, for a few seconds at a time.
No phone from your household answered. They have to be within a few metres with Sprout open. Sending a file works from anywhere.
This phone has no Bluetooth, so it can only exchange files.
Bluetooth is off. Turn it on and try again.
Sprout needs permission to find nearby devices. It is only used to spot the household\'s phones, never your location.
This phone\'s version of Android is too old for this, so it exchanges files instead.
Bluetooth refused to start the search. Turning Bluetooth off and on again usually clears it; otherwise, sending a file always works.
The first exchange has a question to answer. Open a file sent from the other phone once, and after that this works on its own.
Add a baby to see how their days add up.
Nothing logged over this period yet. Feeds, sleep and changes are added up here, day by day.
Log a weight or a measurement to see the curve.
Outside the WHO band (P3–P97), around %1$s. Worth a word at the next appointment.
The WHO curves shown here stop at two years.

Shaded: the WHO child growth standards, 3rd to 97th percentile — warm below the median, cool above it. Both references are shown, girls plain and boys hatched, because Sprout never asks a baby\'s sex. One measurement means little on its own; what a doctor reads is the shape of the line over months. This is not medical advice.

Shaded: the WHO child growth standards for %1$s, 3rd to 97th percentile — warm below the median, cool above it. This choice is not saved: Sprout never asks a baby\'s sex, you are only picking the curve on screen. One measurement means little on its own; what a doctor reads is the shape of the line over months. This is not medical advice.
A solid meal can now say what was in it, and the First foods page gathers every food your baby has met: how many times, the first time and the last. Known allergies have a place of their own too.
The whole household at a glance: for each baby, how long since they were fed, slept and changed, and anything that\'s running right now.

Start a breastfeed from the dashboard: the main button is the breast the last feed didn\'t start on, and the other one is beside it. The tiles open each log, and “Today” adds up the day so far. With more than one baby, tap a card to open that baby\'s own tab. To choose which tiles show and in which order, open “Customise home” in Settings; a tile you switch off waits under “More”.\n\nA feed on the timer, or a baby asleep, shows at the top with a button to open it or to say they woke up. Twins can feed at the same time: each running feed has a row of its own, with the baby\'s name.

Some cards only appear when there\'s something to say: the daily check-in, a note around the ages growth spurts are common, a medicine with a wait running, and what\'s new after an update. None of them stands in your way. The icons at the top open your babies and the settings.
One baby on their own: the same view the dashboard shows when there\'s only one child, for the baby you picked.
Start a breastfeed, open a log from the tiles, see today\'s totals, or go on to the statistics and to “Share a record”. To switch to another baby, tap their card on the dashboard.
This tab appears once there are two or more babies, and it wears the name of the one you picked. Every log you open from here is that baby\'s.
What the logs add up to, day by day: feeds, sleep and nappies, and growth against the WHO standards.

Choose 7, 30 or 90 days. Each card shows a daily average and a bar for every day; on the feeding card, pick which figure to draw. Tap a bar to see what that day was made of, and drag sideways or use the arrows to go back in time. The charts move together.\n\nOn the growth card, tap a measurement to read it against the curves.

Averages cover completed days only, so a half-lived today can\'t drag them down, and a day with nothing logged counts as zero. The window never reaches back before the birth.\n\nThe shaded band is the WHO standards from the 3rd to the 97th percentile. Sprout never asks a baby\'s sex, so each measurement is read against both the girls\' and the boys\' curves and given as a span, such as P22–P34. Choosing girls or boys only changes the curve on screen, and isn\'t saved.
Your own corner: pumping, your wellbeing and the daily check-in, the things that are about you rather than about a baby.
Open “Pumping” for your sessions and the milk stash, “Wellbeing” to look back at how you\'ve been, or the check-in to answer today\'s few questions.

These are yours, not a baby\'s, so deleting a baby leaves them as they are. Your wellbeing and check-ins never leave this phone. If you turn the daily check-in off in Settings, both disappear from here and everything you noted is kept.
Every feed for the baby you picked — breast, bottle and solids — newest first, and the live timer for a breastfeed.

“Start left” or “Start right” opens the timer. Switch sides as you go, tap “Pause” for a burp or a nappy, then “Resume left” or “Resume right”, whichever breast comes next. Tap “Stop & save” when the feed is over.\n\nTap + to log a feed after the fact, a bottle or a meal. “Details” on a breastfeed shows each stretch with its times.

A break is not time at the breast: the clock stops while you\'re paused, and a saved feed ends when its last stretch ended. Leaving the timer doesn\'t stop it. Each baby has a timer of its own, so twins can feed at the same time, and a running feed can also show outside the app, with the same buttons, if you turn that on in Settings.\n\nIf you saved a feed and started again a short while later, the second one may offer “Join with previous”. It asks before it changes anything, and Sprout never joins feeds on its own: only you know whether they were one feed.
Your pumping sessions, and the milk stash: how much is in the fridge, in the freezer or out at room temperature right now.
Tap + after a session to log how much and where it went. When stored milk is drunk or thrown away, tap “Mark as used” and it leaves the stash.

The stash only counts milk that can still be given: used milk, and milk kept longer than the rough guide on this page, is left out of the totals, though its entry stays in the history. Pumping belongs to you rather than to a baby. It\'s shared with your household unless you switch off “Share expressed milk” on the sharing page.
Your baby\'s sleeps, naps and nights alike, newest first.

Tap + to log a sleep. If the baby is still asleep, switch off “Already woke up” and the sleep keeps running; tap “Woke up” on its card, or on the dashboard, when they wake. Where they slept and how they were lying are optional: tap a choice again to clear it.

A sleep that runs past midnight counts towards both days in the statistics, and once as a time settled on the day it began. Sprout records where and how your baby slept and makes no comment on it. To change a sleep, delete it and log it again.
Every nappy change for the baby you picked, newest first.
Tap + and tick “Urine”, “Stool” or both. For a stool you can pick its colour from the swatches, or leave it out.

The colour is kept as you picked it, and Sprout makes nothing of it. Changes add up on the dashboard and in the statistics, where a change with both counts once. To change an entry, delete it and log it again.
Your baby\'s measurements — weight, height and head circumference — whenever they\'re taken.
Tap + and fill in whichever you have: one is enough. Weight is in grams, height and head in centimetres. From the second weight on, a small chart shows the trend.
To see the measurements against the WHO growth curves, open “Trends”. Measurements are shared with your household and go into the record for a doctor. To change one, delete it and add it again.
Courses on a calendar: something given every day, every week or every few days, from a start date until it ends.

Tap + to add one: its name, a dose if you like, how often, the times of day and the dates. “Remind me” sends a notification at each time; switch it off if you\'d rather not. Tap a treatment to change it.

A treatment is a plan, not a record of each dose: Sprout reminds you, but doesn\'t note whether a dose was given. A medicine given only when it\'s needed belongs in “As needed” instead. Courses that have ended move to the bottom of the list.
Medicines given only when they\'re needed, and the question that matters at 3 a.m.: can another dose be given yet?

Tap + to set a medicine up with the figures your prescriber or the leaflet gave you: the shortest wait between doses, a usual wait if there is one, and a daily maximum if you were given one. Then tap “Give a dose” each time it\'s given.\n\nTap a medicine to change its figures, and a dose in the list to correct its time or amount.

The colour is arithmetic on your own figures, never advice. Red: the shortest wait isn\'t over, or the day\'s maximum is used up. Amber: allowed, but sooner than your usual wait. Green: nothing left to wait for. Each colour also has its own icon and its own sentence.\n\n“No set gap” means you were given no wait at all, not a wait of zero: only the daily maximum counts. Sprout knows nothing about any medicine, and “Give a dose” always works, whatever the colour.
Every food your baby has met at a solid meal, one line each, and the allergies your family knows about.

Log a meal with + and list what was in it, from Sprout\'s list or in your own words. For each food, say whether it was a taste or a serving and, if you noticed, how it went. Each food then gets its own line here: how many times it was offered, tastes and servings apart, and the first and last time.\n\n“Details” shows the meals a food was in. “Correct” turns a food into another on every meal of this baby\'s, such as a name you typed into the same food from the list. “Note an allergy” adds one at the top, and “Share the list” makes a one-page PDF of them.

A taste counts as an offer. There\'s no target, no order to follow and no grade: the counts are only what was logged. Sprout\'s list is just names, with no ages and no food marked as an allergen.\n\nSprout never suggests an allergy and never stops you logging a food: one you noted shows “Allergy noted”, and nothing more. If you think your baby reacted to something, ask a doctor.
How you\'re doing, for you alone: your mood and, if you gave birth or are breastfeeding, your recovery. Today\'s check-in, and the history over time.

The daily check-in asks a few questions, one at a time; “Not now” leaves it for later. On “Wellbeing” you can add an entry yourself and look back. A question you\'d rather not be asked can be stopped with “Don\'t ask me this anymore”, or in Settings.

Nothing here leaves this phone: it isn\'t shared with your household and isn\'t in the record for a doctor. The check-in waits on the dashboard and is never a notification. Turning it off in Settings keeps everything you\'ve noted.
The babies Sprout keeps a record for, whether one, twins or siblings.

Tap “Add a baby” and give a name and a date of birth. “Make active” picks the baby the logs open on. You can edit a name or a birth date at any time.\n\n“Stop tracking” hides a baby from the dashboard and keeps their history; bring them back from “Not tracking” whenever you like.
Deleting a baby is for good: everything logged for them is erased, on this phone and, at the next exchange, on the household\'s other phones. Your pumping and your wellbeing are yours, so they stay.
One record for every phone in the household — the other parent\'s, a grandparent\'s — with no account and no server.

Tap “Invite a phone” and send the invitation through an app you trust; on the other phone, tap “Open an invitation I was sent”. Both phones then show the same six-character household code: read it to each other once.\n\nAfter that, “Send my entries” and “Open a file I was sent” bring phones up to date from anywhere. Where this phone offers it, Sprout can also exchange on its own over Bluetooth when you\'re together with Sprout open.

Everything about the babies travels, and the milk stash too unless you switch off “Share expressed milk”. Your wellbeing and check-ins never do. Everyone in the household sees everything shared and can add to it.\n\nRemoving a phone changes the household\'s key, so every phone that stays needs a fresh invitation; the removed phone keeps what it already has. A phone restored from a backup arrives with the record but not in the household: send it a new invitation.
A record of what you\'ve logged for one baby, to hand to a doctor: a PDF to read or print, and a spreadsheet of the entries.

Pick the period, whose exact dates are shown before anything is made, and choose what to include. Then tap “PDF report” or “Spreadsheet” and pick where to send it. “Protect with a password” puts both files in one encrypted zip.

The document states what was logged and interprets nothing. The WHO reference you pick is for this file only and forgotten when you leave; by default both are used and shown as a span. Notes are left out unless you include them, and pumping and your wellbeing are never in it.\n\nThe files are made on this phone and go nowhere until you send them. Sprout keeps no copy of the password: give it in person or by phone, not with the file.
How Sprout works on this phone: its language, reminders, the daily check-in, and sharing with your household.

Choose a language, or keep the phone\'s. Turn on “Feeding reminders” for a nudge when it\'s been a while since a feed, and “Growth spurt alerts” for a heads-up when a typical growth spurt period begins. You can also show a breastfeed you\'re timing outside the app — in the notifications or on the lock screen — with its buttons. “Customise home” chooses which logs the dashboard shows, and in which order. Switch the daily check-in, or any of its questions, on or off. “Household sharing” is where phones are paired.

Feeding reminders, growth spurt alerts and a running feed outside the app stay off until you turn them on, and the check-in is never a notification. These settings belong to this phone and aren\'t shared. The links at the bottom open a donation page in your browser; a donation unlocks nothing, because everything is already here.
Pumping, your wellbeing and the daily check-in.
Sessions, and what is in the fridge.
Your mood and recovery, over time.
Done for today — open it to look back.

Sprout is free, open-source and always will be — every feature is here whether or not you ever give a penny. If it has helped you through the early weeks and you\'d like to chip in towards its development, these open in your browser.
A one-off tip, no account needed.
No browser found to open the page.
A record of what you have logged for %1$s, to hand to a doctor. Both files are made on this phone.
Picking one prints a single centile instead of a span. Sprout still never asks a baby\'s sex, never stores it, and forgets this choice when you leave the screen.
One row per day at the end
The free text typed on entries
Sprout couldn\'t write the file. There may be no room left on the phone.
The file is written on this phone and goes nowhere until you choose where to send it. Sprout still has no internet permission.
Feeding, sleep, nappies and growth as recorded by the family
Every figure here is a count or a total of entries the family typed in. Nothing is estimated, nothing is inferred, and nothing in this document is an assessment.
Averages are over the %1$d completed days in the period; %2$s is counted in the totals and left out of the averages.
Bottle volume covers the %1$d bottles of %2$d that had an amount recorded.
Solid amounts cover the %1$d feeds of %2$d that were weighed.
Time at the breast per day (hours)
%1$s times settled per day · longest single sleep %2$s
Stool colour, where it was recorded: %1$s
Weight (kg), against the WHO 3rd–97th centile band
Medicines given when needed, and every dose in the period
Doses as they were logged, against the limits the parent entered from a prescriber or a leaflet. Sprout applies no limits of its own and draws no conclusion from these figures.
Each food offered in the period, with its count

Each food as it was listed at a meal: how many meals in the period included it, how many were a taste and how many a serving, and how it went when the parent noted it. “First offered” is the first meal it was ever logged in, which may be before the period. Sprout records no reactions and draws no conclusion from these figures.

Sprout does not ask a baby\'s sex. Each measurement is read against both WHO references and printed as the span between them; the true centile is one of the two ends. A dash means the measurement was not taken. One measurement means little on its own — what a doctor reads is the shape of the line over months.

Every centile above is read against the WHO reference for %1$s, because that is what was chosen when this report was made. Sprout does not ask a baby\'s sex, holds none, and has not kept this choice. A dash means the measurement was not taken. One measurement means little on its own — what a doctor reads is the shape of the line over months.
A scheduled dose, when less often than daily

Courses as they were scheduled in the app, on the same dates as the rest of this report. Sprout does not record whether an individual dose was given, so this is the plan rather than an administration record.
A period longer than 92 days is listed by week rather than by day; each row totals the days it covers.

Produced by Sprout on the family\'s phone, from entries they made themselves. It is a log, not a medical record, and contains no assessment of any kind. Sprout has no internet access, and this file exists only because someone chose to share it.
Nothing was logged in this period.
Both files in one encrypted zip
Give the password to the doctor in person or over the phone — not in the same message as the file. Sprout keeps no copy of it and cannot recover it for you.
Encrypted with AES-256. It opens with 7-Zip, WinZip, Keka or most Android file managers — the unzip built into Windows and macOS cannot open it.
No foods yet. Log a solid meal with the + button and list what was in it — each food gets its own count here.
Each food you list gets its own count under First foods.
What was it? Choose a food from the list, or one already logged. Every meal of this baby\'s that lists it will name it that way — how it was given and how it went stay as they were.
Add the day it was noticed
Leave this off for something you have noticed yourselves.
Sprout keeps what you note here and marks the food on every meal. It does not diagnose anything: if you think your baby reacted to a food, ask a doctor. The notes appear on the list you share.
As noted by the family in Sprout. “Confirmed by a health professional” is the family’s own record that a professional confirmed it. Sprout does not diagnose, and this list is not a medical document.
What the baby is noted as allergic to, whatever the period
